races.name: GAIN Equine Nutrition Irish European Breeders Fund Fillies Maiden
Dubai Duty Free Rockingham Handicap (Premier Handicap)

runners_data.name: Gazelle d'Or
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with solid Curragh form at 5f-6f on Good, two recent placed efforts suggest she's primed; sits just off the leader ideally and Colin Keane's booking on Likedbymike rather than here is a slight concern, though Wayne Lordan is a capable replacement.

runners_data.name: Toca Madera
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner in this field who should lead uncontested; David O'Meara's string is firing (8 wins from 63 in 14 days) and Tudhope rides, but the STYLE_FIT flag signals he may be racing outside his natural role if rivals crowd him early — watch for his settling.

runners_data.name: Likedbymike
runners_data.note: Colin Keane takes the mount on this consistent hold-up type who has placed five times from six runs at 5f on Good; capable of a sustained late challenge if the pace holds up, and the 10/15 similar-going strike rate adds confidence.

runners_data.name: Erosandpsyche
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old veteran hold-up type with a visor and a solid Curragh record at 5f on Good (3-3 in recent history); rarely wins these days (one win in seven on similar going) but threads into the frame regularly and is not without each-way appeal.

runners_data.name: Stag Night
runners_data.note: Prominent racer whose form on Good is limited (7/15 similar-going) but who has course and distance experience and placed at 5f recently; best when able to slot in just off the pace, and the McCreery yard has had a quiet 14 days (0 from 17).

runners_data.name: Eclairage
runners_data.note: Prominent type returning on Good to Firm which suits, but a 7th last time at this course and distance on identical conditions tempers enthusiasm; the 7lb claimer Terry Casey is a negative at this level and the form string shows inconsistency.

runners_data.name: Kerdos
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with zero wins and zero places from nine runs on similar going (0W/0P) — the data here is damning; Jack Kearney's 3lb claim helps with the burden but this horse struggles to land a blow in competitive sprint handicaps.

runners_data.name: Sarahmae
runners_data.note: In sharp form with back-to-back wins at 5f and carrying momentum into this race (LR: 9 days); a prominent type who can press the leader on fast ground, and the Hogan yard is ticking over with 2 from 10 in 14 days — one of the more interesting profiles here.

runners_data.name: Dark Ace
runners_data.note: Won twice at 6f on Standard (Dundalk) and most recent Curragh run was only 2 from 15 on similar going — the jump from all-weather to Good to Firm turf at 5f is the question mark; Adam Caffrey keeps the ride and a 43-day break adds a trace of freshness.

runners_data.name: Red Evolution
runners_data.note: Progressive prominent type who won twice on Good going earlier in the season; the 107-day break is a significant concern, but O'Callaghan and McMonagle are a sharp combination and the 2W/5P record on similar going suggests ability in these conditions.

runners_data.name: Moltophino
runners_data.note: Has genuine front-running tendencies that go with his prominent profile, but the field density pushes him into a midfield position he won't enjoy; modest recent form (9th, 20th) on Good at 6f suggests he's struggling at present regardless of position.

runners_data.name: Back Down Under
runners_data.note: A natural prominent racer by inclination, nudged into midfield on the map because the front is oversubscribed; his 6f form dominates his history and the drop to 5f here is a question — his 5f experience is limited and the style displacement compounds the challenge.

runners_data.name: Cuban Grey
runners_data.note: Genuine speed horse who wants to be prominent but cannot get there in this field; his one 5f Curragh win (OR=78 level) is on record but he's been finding 5f on Good tough of late (9th last time), and being forced wide or back will blunt his chance further.

runners_data.name: Buddy Batt
runners_data.note: Multiple 5f winner on Standard ground who gets bumped back to a midfield slot here despite his front-running instincts; the soft-to-standard winning profile doesn't map cleanly to Good to Firm turf, and his form on similar going is limited (6/15 sample, 1W/1P).

runners_data.name: Shadow Of The Moon
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with an excellent small sample on similar going (4/6 in-the-frame) and a recent placed effort at 5f on Soft; the step up to Good to Firm is a query but the raw ability is there, and a clean run through from the rear could see her finish strongly.

runners_data.name: Genesis
runners_data.note: True hold-up type mapped to midfield due to overcrowding at the rear — his best form has come at 6f on Good and the drop to 5f is a potential stumbling block; the STYLE_FIT flag and trip concern combine to make this a low-probability winning prospect.

runners_data.name: Harry's Hill
runners_data.note: An 8-year-old hold-up type who wears a hood and contests 5f on Good regularly without winning; his 1W/2P from 11 similar-going runs over a long career suggests he plugs on honestly without threatening at the top of handicap company.

races.paceDynamic: Toca Madera is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the early lead, should settle into a comfortable, uncontested rhythm from the off on Good to Firm ground over this sharp 5f at the Curragh. The pace will be honest but not suicidal — a lone leader dictating on fast ground through the early stages creates a rail-skimming, compressed race where the leader controls tempo and rivals must come from off the pace to close. This field holds significantly more prominent-running types than the track can accommodate at the front — Moltophino, Back Down Under, Cuban Grey, and Buddy Batt are all genuine prominent/front types who will be squeezed back into midfield roles against their natural instincts, adding a scrimmaging dimension to the early stages. The race shape strongly favours horses who can sit just behind the leader in the slipstream and sustain their run — true prominent types who actually secure that position (Gazelle d'Or, Stag Night, Sarahmae) and progressive horses capable of a powerful late sweep from mid-division are the profiles to focus on; deep closers face the most daunting task as the leader sets a controlled, makeable pace with no pace collapse to exploit.

scenarios.title: Toca Madera Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Toca Madera bowls clear from stall and no rival forces a contested pace, allowing a solo front-running display.
scenarios.body: If Toca Madera bowls clear from stall and no rival forces a contested pace, allowing a solo front-running display.

scenarios.trigger: If the jostling pack of prominent types who secure second and third berths build relentless pressure and the leader is caught in the final 100 yards.
scenarios.body: If the jostling pack of prominent types who secure second and third berths build relentless pressure and the leader is caught in the final 100 yards.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Sweeper Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Toca Madera either goes off too fast or fades from its efforts and a gap appears down the outside in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If Toca Madera either goes off too fast or fades from its efforts and a gap appears down the outside in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos From Crowded Midfield
scenarios.trigger: If the redistribution of multiple prominent types into midfield causes a bunched, scrimmaging race with trouble in running that scrambles the result.
scenarios.body: If the redistribution of multiple prominent types into midfield causes a bunched, scrimmaging race with trouble in running that scrambles the result.

watchPoints.text: Sarahmae — entering in sharp form after back-to-back wins and likely to press Toca Madera from a prominent position; if she can match strides with the leader early, she could overpower Toca Madera in the closing stages.

Toca Madera — watch for whether Gazelle d'Or, Stag Night, or Sarahmae push up aggressively in the first furlong; any early pressure could transform this from a controlled solo lead into a contested burn-up that changes the entire race shape.

Moltophino, Back Down Under, Cuban Grey — all natural prominent types who will be squeezed for position in the first furlong; scrimmaging among these three in the middle of the track could cause trouble for horses immediately behind them.

Red Evolution — the 107-day absence is the key flag; if McMonagle lets him run fresh and he bounces back to his early-season form on Good, he's dangerously well-handicapped, but race-fitness from a long break at 5f on fast ground is a genuine risk.

Dark Ace — sole runner whose primary winning form is on all-weather Standard surfaces (two wins at Dundalk); monitor in-running to see if the Good to Firm turf appears to suit or whether he struggles to replicate his synthetic form on grass.

races.name: Jebel Ali Racecourse & Stables Dash Stakes (Listed)

runners_data.name: Big Gossey
runners_data.note: Veteran nine-year-old with strong prominent style and two placed efforts at 6f on Good recently; Charles O'Brien sends him in on a tight 36-day turnaround and his sim-going record (0W3P from 11 comparable runs) shows he hits the frame without winning, making him a reliable each-way threat rather than a likely winner.

runners_data.name: Bodhi Bear
runners_data.note: In excellent recent form having won over 5f Good last time out for J A Stack; Seamie Heffernan takes over and the trainer has sent two winners out in the past 14 days, but stepping to 6f from a 5f win on Good To Firm ground is the key question given his three wins have all come at 5f.

runners_data.name: Tango Flare
runners_data.note: Outstanding course-and-distance profile — five of his last five runs have been at 6f on Good, recording two wins and never finishing out of the first two; Patrick Foley's gelding wears a tongue tie and visor, and his natural hold-up style means he needs a genuine pace to run into, which this race is likely to provide.

runners_data.name: California Dreamer
runners_data.note: Steps back in trip from 7f-8f races to 6f for the first time in this dataset, and all five recent runs have been at 7f or further; the drop to a sprint trip on Good To Firm is a significant query, and his hold-up style in a race with limited genuine pace compression at the rear makes this a tough assignment.

runners_data.name: Fregada
runners_data.note: Has recorded six finishes of sixth or worse in her last six runs and her recent form string offers little encouragement; she is a genuine hold-up type by nature but is unlikely to find the clean passage from midfield that her style requires in this competitive field, and the STYLE_FIT flag appropriately tempers expectations.

runners_data.name: Little Queenie
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old mare with a mixed recent record including a win over 6f at Stow and placed efforts, trained by Paul Flynn who has sent two winners out in 14 days; by inclination a hold-up horse, she will find the pace map works against getting her natural position, and her best recent form has come on Soft or Standard rather than Good To Firm.

runners_data.name: Temperance
runners_data.note: Returns from a massive 353-day absence, which is the dominant factor here; she has winning form at 6f on Good and wore a hood in her last run, but fitness after nearly a year off must be a serious concern regardless of her natural hold-up style, which also faces the same congestion issues as the other closers in this field.

runners_data.name: Oh Cecelia
runners_data.note: Three-year-old filly who has been in consistent form with a recent win over 5f on Soft and placed efforts at 6f; Shane Foley takes the ride for K J Condon, she wears a hood, and the step up to Listed class is the test — her hold-up style is genuine and she is one of the more believable late finishers if a gap materialises.

runners_data.name: Silk Braid
runners_data.note: The top-rated runner (OR 120) in this Listed sprint with only two career runs — a win and a second, both at 6f Good at the Curragh — for the powerful Ger Lyons/Colin Keane combination; confirmed front-runner who has the class to back up her prominent style, but relative inexperience is the caveat, and the STYLE_FIT flag reflects she is being asked to lead rather than race in a tracking role.

runners_data.name: Tahcawin
runners_data.note: Consistent three-year-old with a course win at 6f Good and placed efforts over the trip; Gary Carroll partners for Joseph Murphy, and his prominent style makes him ideally suited to tracking Silk Braid from the front, though a modest recent run (third of 3f) and form drop-off in his last three suggest he may need things to go very right.

races.paceDynamic: Silk Braid is the confirmed front-runner here, and with Colin Keane in the saddle for Ger Lyons, she is likely to be ridden positively from her draw to establish an uncontested lead on Good to Firm ground at the Curragh over 6f. Big Gossey, Bodhi Bear, and Tahcawin are genuine prominent types who will push forward and track Silk Braid, creating a compressed front pack but not an outright speed duel — the pace should be honest rather than suicidal. The field contains more hold-up and prominent types than can all slot into their preferred positions; Fregada, Little Queenie, and Temperance are true hold-up horses but have been mapped to midfield given the congestion at the rear, meaning they are unlikely to get the clean late run their style demands. This race shape — a single front-runner dictating a controlled but honest gallop on fast ground — strongly favours horses who can race prominently and sustain their effort through the final furlong, rather than those relying on a pronounced pace collapse to deliver a finishing kick.

scenarios.title: Silk Braid Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Silk Braid secures the lead without serious early pressure and controls the tempo at a true but manageable pace.
scenarios.body: If Silk Braid secures the lead without serious early pressure and controls the tempo at a true but manageable pace.

scenarios.body: If Big Gossey and Bodhi Bear press Silk Braid hard enough to drain her finishing reserves in the final furlong.

scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong and a clean passage materialises for one of the true finishers in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: If the pace is genuinely strong and a clean passage materialises for one of the true finishers in the closing stages.

scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final furlong and a horse tracking from mid-division picks up the pieces.

watchPoints.text: Silk Braid's 64-day absence is the main vulnerability — watch her paddock condition and early stride pattern to gauge whether Keane can establish a controlled lead or if the layoff has left her short of peak fitness.

Big Gossey, Bodhi Bear, and Tahcawin are all likely to press forward simultaneously — if all three push for position aggressively in the first furlong, the early tempo could be faster than anticipated and undermine Silk Braid's ability to dictate at her own pace.

Tango Flare's hold-up style is his strength but he needs a smooth run from the midfield pack — watch for traffic at the 2f pole where the field is likely to compress; a clean passage through would significantly boost his finishing prospects in a scenario where the pace tells.

Temperance's 353-day layoff is a significant fitness flag — her market position at the off will indicate trainer confidence, but backers should note she has never been sighted in this field's context and represents a major unknown in the pace picture if she shapes to close ground late.

Oh Cecelia is dropping into a field rated significantly higher than her recent wins have come against — the jump to Listed class for a three-year-old on Good To Firm at the Curragh over 6f is a meaningful step up, and how she handles the early pace of this race relative to her previous experiences will determine whether she can repeat recent placed form.

races.name: Dubai Duty Free Derby Festival Handicap (Premier Handicap)

runners_data.name: Lord Massusus
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator for Joseph Murphy who has decent Good-ground form (8/15 runs, one win, one placed); 49 days between runs is worth noting, but apprentice Paddy Harnett (5lb) helps on the weights at OR 98; will need a gap to appear late.|

runners_data.name: Perry Mason
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner and likely to have an uncontested lead; trainer Ahern has a live 14-day record (1/5) and the horse won at 10f on Good last time, stepping back to 1m; controlling the fractions gives him every chance to be in the argument at the line.|

runners_data.name: Far From Dandy
runners_data.note: Won over this C&D last time in handicap company and placed twice in 8f Good-ground races this year, making him course-and-distance proven; Jack Kearney's 3lb claim is a bonus, and the head-gear note (p) suggests he needs to be held up to some degree; a straightforward prominent profile that suits this shape.|

runners_data.name: State Actor
runners_data.note: Has 238 days between runs which is a significant fitness concern at OR 91 in a competitive handicap; Colin Keane's booking is eye-catching, but the horse's last win at 8f on Good came over two years ago and recent form reads 36550 — hard to trust on return.|

runners_data.name: Orandi
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old who has run 21st twice at this trip in recent outings; tongue-tie fitted and the trainer's 14-day record is 0/5 — this profile offers very little encouragement in terms of a competitive chance, though he does carry a small weight.|

runners_data.name: Zarathos
runners_data.note: Back-to-back wins at 7f and 8f on Good ground recently for the in-form Dylan Cunha yard (3/22 over 14 days) makes him the most interesting prominent type; Dylan Browne McMonagle takes the ride, and an OR rise to 90 may not be enough to stop him given the form trajectory of a horse going the right way.|

runners_data.name: Coeur d'Or
runners_data.note: Genuinely wants to race prominently but is mapped to midfield here because the field is overloaded with front-running types — a ten-year-old with tongue and bit headgear now, his recent runs at 9-10f suggest stepping back to 1m is ideal; however, racing against his instincts from a shuffled-back position blunts his chance.|

runners_data.name: Slieve Binnian
runners_data.note: Won twice at 9f and 7f on Good-ground courses and races prominently by nature, but in this field there simply is not room for him to hold that position comfortably; six consecutive out-of-the-money finishes at longer trips suggest the drop back to 1m helps, but the style displacement is a real check on expectations.|

runners_data.name: Booyea
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse for W J Lee and Thomas Gibney whose two recent wins have come on Soft — the step up to Good to Firm ground is a question given his going profile; 24 days between runs is fine, and blinkers fitted, but he needs things to happen late in a race that may not set up for him.|

runners_data.name: Playin Cool
runners_data.note: Won at 9f on Heavy and placed at 7f on Soft, so the jump to Good to Firm on a flat Curragh mile is a going query; a natural prominent runner who is displaced into midfield here, meaning he races out of role — his style-fit score of 0.93 reflects a genuinely compromised tactical position.|

runners_data.name: Pierre Royal
runners_data.note: Won and placed over 8f on Good at the Curragh specifically, so course-and-distance form is solid; Adrian McGuinness's yard has a lively 14-day record (2/30) and Adam Caffrey takes over; naturally prominent but mapped to midfield by redistribution — if he recovers position quickly he remains a legitimate interest.|

runners_data.name: Pretty Omagh Girl
runners_data.note: Won over this exact trip on Good ground last time out for Ben Coen and A Oliver whose stable is operating at 3/15 over 14 days; a natural prominent type displaced into midfield, she is the freshest horse for Coen to aim at this race shape, and her recent winning form over C&D makes her the most dangerous of the redistributed runners if she secures a prominent berth.|

runners_data.name: Red Charlie
runners_data.note: Trainer-ridden angle for Andrew Slattery (4/33 over 14 days) and has one win from five at 7f on Heavy; light-weighted at OR 77 with tongue-tie fitted and hold-up style — Good to Firm ground on a flat mile is not a natural profile fit, though the light weight keeps him in the frame for a place in a bunched finish.|

races.paceDynamic: Perry Mason is the one confirmed front-runner in this 13-runner field and, with no meaningful challenger expected to match him for the early lead, he should dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front on Good to Firm ground over a flat mile at the Curragh. That single-pace-setter dynamic means the tempo is unlikely to be truly searching, which will compress the field through the middle stages and set up a tactical, attritional finish rather than a punishing end-to-end test. The field is loaded with prominent-racing types — Slieve Binnian, Coeur d'Or, Playin Cool, Pierre Royal and Pretty Omagh Girl are all genuine prominent horses who cannot all secure their natural position behind Perry Mason, meaning several will be shuffled back into midfield against their instincts, creating a congested race shape. This race shape overwhelmingly favours horses who can sit just off the controlled pace in second or third — the genuine prominent runners who successfully hold their position close to Perry Mason will have a decisive advantage over the redistributed types racing out of role.

scenarios.body: If Perry Mason dictates a sedate, uncontested gallop and the prominent horses sitting directly behind him sprint off his back in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.body: If Perry Mason goes too slow up front and the race turns into a sprint finish where hold-up horses get a clear run through.

watchPoints.text: Zarathos has won back-to-back over course and distance on Good ground for an in-form yard — watch whether Dylan Browne McMonagle can secure a prominent position in the first half mile before the congested field settles.

Pretty Omagh Girl won over this exact C&D trip last time and Ben Coen is a top jockey — watch how quickly she travels to recover a prominent pitch from her mapped midfield position, because if she does the style-fit concern is greatly reduced.

The cluster of redistributed prominent types — Slieve Binnian, Coeur d'Or, Playin Cool and Pierre Royal — creates a flashpoint entering the first bend; watch for bumping or checking as they all try to assert forward positions that the race shape cannot accommodate simultaneously.

State Actor returns after 238 days off and has not won at this trip on Good since 2022 — despite the Colin Keane booking, the fitness angle is a significant watch point for those opposing at short prices.

Perry Mason's pace in the first two furlongs will be decisive for the whole field shape — watch whether he dawdles and invites a sprint finish, or presses on to establish a true rhythm that tests those racing out of role in midfield.

races.name: Dubai Duty Free International Stakes (Group 3)

runners_data.name: Crown Of Oaks
runners_data.note: William Haggas and Tom Marquand link up with a mare who has won three of her last five starts, but 253 days off the track is a significant concern, and in this field she cannot get her preferred prominent berth — she will be further back than ideal, which blunts her chances considerably.

runners_data.name: Hotazhell
runners_data.note: Shane Foley partners a mare who has consistent place form in this grade and handles Good to Firm well across a big sample; she should be able to hold a prominent position naturally in this field, which puts her in the best tactical spot of any non-Purview runner.

runners_data.name: Purview
runners_data.note: D K Weld's four-year-old is the race's only confirmed front-runner and arrives on the back of back-to-back wins; Colin Keane will control the tempo on ground that suits, and the horse's front-running style here is its natural role — this is where the pace map begins and ends.

runners_data.name: Tiberius Thunder
runners_data.note: The only genuine hold-up horse in the field, Robson De Aguiar's runner has a modest recent form string and needs pace to chase; it gets the right setup but lacks the class to capitalise, having failed to win in ten career starts.

runners_data.name: Trustyourinstinct
runners_data.note: Joseph Patrick O'Brien's six-year-old gelding won over 10f on Good ground last time and has a strong record on similar surfaces; J M Sheridan takes the ride and this horse's natural prominent style should allow it to hold its position without the redistribution issues affecting others.

runners_data.name: Sindria
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle is a high-class jockey but this horse's natural front-running instincts cannot be accommodated in a field this prominent-heavy — it will be asked to race further back than it wants, and its best form over shorter trips on Good to Firm adds a distance query at 1m2f.

runners_data.name: Geryon
runners_data.note: G M Lyons sends out a three-year-old with five consecutive placed finishes, suggesting a consistent if not winning type; the colt is a natural prominent racer who has been pushed into a midfield mapping by the field's composition, and his trainer has had no winners in the last 14 days — modest context.

runners_data.name: Isaac Newton
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore is the standout jockey booking and gives this A P O'Brien three-year-old a big tactical advantage, but the horse wants to race up with the pace and the race shape prevents it — won over 9f on Good last time, so the trip is fine, but being shuffled out of his natural running position is a meaningful disadvantage.

races.paceDynamic: Purview is the confirmed front-runner and, with Colin Keane aboard, will dictate from the front on Good to Firm ground at a sustainable tempo — this is not a horse who will be pressured into a suicidal gallop, and the pace is likely to be honest but controlled. The field is heavily loaded with prominent-style horses: Crown Of Oaks, Sindria, Geryon, and Isaac Newton are all natural early-movers but cannot all occupy the ground they want, meaning several will be shuffled into unnatural midfield positions and will not be racing to their strengths. Hotazhell and Trustyourinstinct are the two horses most likely to genuinely hold their prominent berths alongside Purview, while the redistributed quartet will be racing in roles that compromise their effectiveness. This race shape — a single front-runner controlling a steady pace with genuine prominent types tracking — strongly favours horses that can sit just off the leader, travel comfortably through the race, and produce a sustained challenge over the final two furlongs rather than a sharp turn-of-foot finish from deep.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Hotazhell and Trustyourinstinct both successfully hold prominent positions — if either is pushed wider or back by the crowd of early movers, the race shape changes significantly.

Isaac Newton with Ryan Moore is likely to attempt to recover natural prominent ground from a midfield mapping, which could produce a wide move on the turn and a significant run in the straight — do not dismiss on price.
Crown Of Oaks returns after 253 days off the track for William Haggas; Haggas horses often need a run after a long break, and this flat-race distance after that layoff is a flag on fitness.

The Good to Firm ground (confirmed for 3:20 by the going report) is considerably faster than the listed race going of "Good" — horses with form on faster surfaces are at a premium, and any runner who has previously struggled on quick ground should be treated with added caution.

Geryon's headgear (tongue-tie flagged) and five consecutive runner-up or placed finishes suggest a horse who performs with credit but may lack the winning instinct to convert — note if drifting in the market pre-race.

races.name: Dubai Duty Free Celebration Stakes (Listed)

runners_data.name: Alcantor
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with the licence to dictate here, but his recent form of 446-46 is uninspiring and his similar-going record (3/15, 0 wins, 0 places) is a significant concern on ground this fast; expect him to control the race without being dominated, yet he is vulnerable to the closers he sets up.|

runners_data.name: Cowardofthecounty
runners_data.note: Last-time-out winner over 7f at Good, trained by Joseph O'Brien alongside stablemate Accredited; genuine hold-up profile suits this controlled scenario perfectly, and the step up to a mile should not inconvenience him given his two recent placed efforts at that trip. The 16-day turnaround for O'Brien's yard, firing at 13/63, merits respect.|

runners_data.name: Tokenomics
runners_data.note: A strong candidate given his good-ground form at the mile — three wins from eight similar-ground starts with five places — and he comes here freshened after 49 days off for a trainer (Marnane) who strikes at 1/9 over 14 days, suggesting he is ready. His natural prominent style fits the anticipated race shape without redistribution.|

runners_data.name: Zodiac Bear
runners_data.note: Stepped up from a recent 7f win on Good going; his four-run form sample is small but includes that course win at this trip's shorter neighbour, and Ben Coen takes the ride for J P Murtagh (3/22 over 14 days). The switch to a mile is the key question given his last three runs have all been at seven.|

runners_data.name: Duckadilly
runners_data.note: Three wins from nine Good-ground starts confirm the going holds no fears, but his best form has come when able to stride forward into a prominent position naturally — a scenario less likely here given the traffic ahead of him. Scott McCullagh rides for McLoughlin (0/6 over 14 days), and the redistribution away from his preferred berth is a real tactical cost.|

runners_data.name: Spicy Margarita
runners_data.note: Returned from 86 days off with a moderate recent record and a step back from 10-12f to a mile raises distance questions, given her best form has come at longer trips; however she is a genuine hold-up type whose style is perfectly aligned to the controlled pace scenario, meaning if the class is there the opportunity is real. Donagh O'Connor rides for De Aguiar (1/14 over 14 days).|

runners_data.name: Accredited
runners_data.note: The youngest in the field at three and carrying the lightest weight; Ryan Moore is a powerful booking for A P O'Brien (8/43 over 14 days), and she won over 7f on Soft last time, but her 5/8f/GOO run is the only similar-ground reference. A natural prominent type whose redistribution to a deeper position in the field means Moore will likely need to work harder than ideal to get her into the race.|

races.paceDynamic: Alcantor is the confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger disputing the lead, he is likely to control the tempo at a measured, sustainable clip on Good to Firm ground over a mile at the Curragh. Tokenomics and Zodiac Bear will press into prominent positions just behind him, creating an organised, single-file shape rather than a pressured gallop — the pace will be honest but unlikely to be truly searching. Duckadilly and Accredited are natural prominent types who cannot both secure their preferred berth given Alcantor and Tokenomics already occupy the front rank; one or both will find themselves racing further back than ideal, which reduces their effectiveness. This race shape — a controlled, uncontested lead producing a steady early tempo — strongly favours hold-up horses who can sustain their finish through the final two furlongs, and prominent types disciplined enough to travel close to the pace without burning energy competing for position.

watchPoints.text: Cowardofthecounty's hold-up profile is ideally constructed for the controlled pace Alcantor will set — watch for McDonogh to have him poised in the straight as this race shape directly suits him.

Duckadilly and Accredited are both natural prominent racers and their early position-seeking may briefly elevate the pace — if they bump into each other or Tokenomics chasing Alcantor, the tempo could spike unexpectedly in the first two furlongs.
Tokenomics is 49 days off the track; Marnane's 14-day strike rate of 1/9 suggests readiness, but watch the paddock to confirm he has trained on and is moving freely before committing to his chance.

Zodiac Bear's rise from seven furlongs to a mile is untested in his recent form cycle — watch how Coen positions him in the early stages; if he is pushed wide or forced to race keenly, the step up in trip could expose a stamina question.

Spicy Margarita drops back from 10-12f trips to a mile after 86 days off — if she shows signs of freshness early and travels kindly, her hold-up style could make her a dangerous each-way proposition despite the modest recent form figures.

races.name: Dubai Duty Free Irish Derby (Group 1)

runners_data.name: Action
runners_data.note: Consistent performer with good-ground form figures of 2-2-4 at similar trips, but his naturally prominent style means he faces a direct fight for position against several equally forward-going rivals in this eight-runner field, which could blunt his chance before the race truly begins.

runners_data.name: Benvenuto Cellini
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore takes the ride on an A P O'Brien runner who has won four of five starts including a Group 1, with strong course-relevant form on good ground — he is one of the few horses here whose actual running style matches the position he's been assigned, making him the most structurally sound challenger to Christmas Day.

runners_data.name: Bunyola Bay
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's progressive three-year-old arrives on the back of back-to-back wins but steps sharply up in class and distance simultaneously; his front-running inclinations will see him pushed into the pack by rivals of equal or stronger intent, and the Group 1 test on good-to-firm ground is a significant ask.

runners_data.name: Christmas Day
runners_data.note: The confirmed single front-runner in this field, with Ronan Whelan able to slide into an uncontested lead and control every fraction — his recent Curragh form includes a 1m2f win on good ground, and the step to 1m4f looks well within his stamina profile, putting him in the most tactically privileged position in the race.

runners_data.name: James J Braddock
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle partners a horse who naturally wants to be prominent but must compete with at least three other forward-going types for the same early positions; his best form is on good ground and he has a win and a place at 1m2f, but the 1m4f trip and the crowded early stages are the key unknowns.

runners_data.name: Pierre Bonnard
runners_data.note: Carrying the lowest OR in the field among prominent types and with his last seven runs showing a win and two places from seven on similar going, he has been remapped to a rear position by force of field composition rather than genuine preference — his recent form reads 7-7 in two starts over this distance at Group level, which is a meaningful concern.

runners_data.name: Raaheeb
runners_data.note: Owen Burrows sends over an unbeaten horse (two from two including a 1m win on good ground) who has had 65 days off the track — the freshness could be an asset on fast ground but he is deeply unexposed at this trip and in Group 1 company, making him the most interesting quantity in the field without a defined positional profile to lean on.

runners_data.name: Shaihaan
runners_data.note: Donnacha O'Brien's runner has a mixed record on good ground (zero wins from three similar-conditions starts) and his natural desire to race prominently will place him in the same crowded early group as several rivals — Tom Marquand will have his work cut out finding a clean passage once the field bunches heading to the first turn.

races.paceDynamic: Christmas Day is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine rival to press him, Ronan Whelan can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front — this is not a race where the pace will be artificially hot. Good to firm ground at the Curragh over 1m4f rewards relaxed, well-balanced racing and a steady tempo suits a horse who can quicken off it rather than one who needs grinding attrition to wear rivals down. The field is loaded with prominent-racing types — Action, Bunyola Bay, James J Braddock, and Shaihaan are all natural front-to-midfield horses who will be competing for the same early real estate, creating a crowded prominent group even if the overall tempo remains modest. This race shape strongly favours a horse that can settle just behind Christmas Day without spending energy fighting for position, has tactical speed to move smoothly into contention turning in, and possesses a sharp enough turn of foot to pounce on a pace that has never truly been pushed — in short, a classy hold-up or true midfield runner with a clean passage is best placed, though with so few genuine hold-up types in this field, the winner is most likely to come from just off the pace rather than from deep in the rear. The redistribution of Action, Bunyola Bay, James J Braddock, and Shaihaan into artificial midfield/hold-up slots reflects that the field holds more forward-going horses than the race can accommodate — Christmas Day and Benvenuto Cellini are the likeliest to actually secure their natural forward positions.

scenarios.body: If Christmas Day's controlled pace turns the race into a sprint from two furlongs out and one horse travels sweetly just off the leader throughout without expending unnecessary energy.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closer Benefits

scenarios.body: If the congestion among the prominent group burns excessive early energy and the genuine pace is faster than anticipated, leaving front-runners and near-leaders flattening out.

watchPoints.text: Christmas Day — watch whether Ronan Whelan is able to find the lead cleanly from stalls 1-4; if any horse disputes early with him, the controlled tempo evaporates and the entire race shape resets.

Benvenuto Cellini — Ryan Moore must avoid being swallowed by the prominent-horse traffic; if he gets squeezed into the pack rather than sitting second cleanly, his chance in Scenario A/B is materially reduced.

James J Braddock and Action — both are natural front-runners who cannot all get their position; watch the first two furlongs to see which, if either, manages to secure a forward slot and which drops back into a compromised mid-pack position.
Raaheeb — 65 days off the track with only two career starts; watch the paddock and early strides for any signs of greenness or freshness on ground faster than anything he has encountered before.

Pierre Bonnard — his two runs over this exact 1m4f trip have produced 7th-place finishes; watch whether he settles better than those outings suggested or whether this distance remains beyond his current ability level.

races.name: Tulfarris Hotel And Golf Resort Maddenstown Handicap (Premier Handicap)

runners_data.name: Listentodwindblow
runners_data.note: Front-runner for JP O'Brien with Declan McDonogh up, tongue tie fitted; won over 8f on Good last time and has similar-going form but faces two rivals who will push him immediately, making this a burning lead battle that will test his stamina over the extra furlong.

runners_data.name: Satoyama
runners_data.note: JP O'Brien's second string ridden by Dylan Browne McMonagle, prominent style, back after 28 days; two from three on Good ground and steps up to 9f for the first time which suits his patient but forward-placed manner in a race where the front will blow.

runners_data.name: Bobby McGee
runners_data.note: Hat-trick winner in excellent form for Noel Meade, six from seven on similar going, sits prominently and travels well; the step to 9f should not inconvenience him and Chris Hayes knows how to ride a well-found prominent horse into a pace-collapse finish.

runners_data.name: Summer Is Tomorrow
runners_data.note: Prominent type for JP O'Brien who has been freshened up over 21 days; visored last time and has Good-ground form, though recent 9th over 9f on Good is a flag — this trip may be ideal but current form does not inspire confidence.

runners_data.name: Antigua
runners_data.note: Front-runner with the significant advantage of Ryan Moore, tongue tie and blinkers, drops back from 10-12f trips; has beaten rivals on Good ground at 10f and Moore's ability to find a rhythm and shield him from the other leaders is the key variable in this race's shape.

runners_data.name: Brownstown
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse for Gavin Cromwell, freshened 27 days; placed at 8f on Good and the burning pace genuinely plays to his late-closing profile, though he has zero wins from seven similar-going attempts which is an honesty note that must temper enthusiasm.

runners_data.name: How'sthebai
runners_data.note: Front-runner for GM Lyons under Colin Keane, won over 9f on Soft and at 8f on Standard but only one similar-going run on record; will lock horns with Listentodwindblow and Antigua immediately and is unlikely to dominate this three-way lead contest.

runners_data.name: Rolltight
runners_data.note: Ben Coen takes over on this JP Murtagh-trained colt who has won and placed over 8f on Good; three from three on Good ground and a prominent, accurate style makes him an each-way type if the pace demolishes the front three in the straight.

runners_data.name: Manton Bay
runners_data.note: Prominent runner for David Marnane, placed at 10f on Good which is a distance pointer; quiet stable form (1/9 in 14 days) and the inexperienced Luke McAteer ride are negatives, but if the gallop suits he has the stamina profile to stay on.

runners_data.name: King Of Earth
runners_data.note: Tom Marquand travels from England for William Haggas, who is in strong form (12/56 in 14 days); prominent/patient type who won at 8f on Standard and has placed twice on Soft — the Curragh at Good to Firm over 9f stretches his comfort zone but Haggas trip-up runners often outperform price.

runners_data.name: Stars Will Shine
runners_data.note: Prominent type for Noel Meade, won over 7f on Good, placed at 6f — the step to 9f looks a trip question and the yard's second string behind Bobby McGee; best watched from a pace perspective rather than relied upon.

runners_data.name: Monvoe
runners_data.note: Roger Cody's filly has been prolific over 8f on Good ground with three wins in the grade, naturally races prominently; placed into a hold-up mapping position because the field is short of genuine closers, but her true racing style involves taking a forward pitch and she should be interpreted accordingly.

runners_data.name: Cherry Hill Girl
runners_data.note: Hold-up type for Andrew Slattery, placed at 10f on Good and 8f on Soft; the burning pace suits her style on paper but the recent form string of 3-7743 tells a story of progressive decline and she will need the front to collapse comprehensively to feature.

runners_data.name: Sanctijude
runners_data.note: Good recent winner at 8f on Good for W McCreery; a natural prominent racer whose position is pushed rearward by the volume of pace in this field — the note to take is that if he finds any forward berth he becomes dangerous, but racing genuinely from behind is not his game.

runners_data.name: Anushka
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead's filly, three wins over shorter trips and has placed twice on Good; instinctively wants to race handily but the sheer number of forward horses means she will be squeezed into a position she has not trained for — temper confidence accordingly.

runners_data.name: Punica Granatum
runners_data.note: Twice placed over 8f on Good for Mrs Harrington with Shane Foley, a reliable mid-order prominent racer; the crowded pace map leaves her without her natural front-half berth, and while she stays on honestly, benefiting from this race shape from an unnatural position is a stretch.

runners_data.name: Liberation Date
runners_data.note: Last ran only two days ago — that brutally short turnaround for Jack Foley's filly is the headline concern regardless of anything else; a natural prominent racer squeezed to the rear by the field's pace density, but fitness and freshness are the overriding questions here.

runners_data.name: Ryefield Dasher
runners_data.note: Thomas Gibney's 77-rated filly with zero wins from four on Good or similar going; pushed back from her natural prominent position by the crowd at the front, and with modest form figures (6/5/4/10) there is little evidence to suggest she can win from any position in this field.

races.paceDynamic: Listentodwindblow, How'sthebai, and Antigua will all contest the front end from the outset, creating a genuine three-way battle for the lead over 1m1f on Good to Firm ground at the Curragh — a strong, pressured gallop is virtually certain from the first furlong. This pace dynamic will stretch the field early, burn off the leaders before the straight, and turn the race into a stamina examination in the closing stages. Prominent types who can sit just off the hot pace — Satoyama, Bobby McGee, and Rolltight — are best placed to pounce as the front trio tie each other up, making a patient but forward-placed runner the most favoured profile in this shape. The field holds significantly more prominent/front-running types than can physically secure their natural position; Sanctijude, Anushka, Punica Granatum, Liberation Date, and Ryefield Dasher are all genuine prominent racers who will be shuffled back against their will, meaning their pace and position maps are distorted by circumstance rather than preference.

watchPoints.text: Watch Antigua's early positioning — if Ryan Moore slots him into a controlled lead rather than fighting with Listentodwindblow and How'sthebai, the entire pace dynamic shifts from a burn-out scenario to a manufactured gallop that dramatically improves Antigua's winning chance.

Bobby McGee's draw and Noel Meade's form make him the most credible beneficiary of a pace collapse — watch whether Chris Hayes gets him into fourth or fifth in the first furlong, as any farther back and the Curragh straight may not provide enough cover for a big run.

Liberation Date ran just two days ago — monitor any market drift or stable comment before the off, as the extremely short turnaround is an abnormal risk flag that could indicate something unexpected or simply an opportunistic entry on very quick ground.

Monvoe's true style is prominent, not hold-up — if she bursts forward out of the gate and takes her natural position, her strong Good-ground form (three wins in that condition) makes her a live threat that her mapped position significantly undersells.

With three confirmed front-runners and at least five more prominent types crammed into the midfield against their will, watch the first two furlongs carefully — a chaotic, bunching start at a flat Curragh over 9f is a real possibility and any interference or shuffling back in the early stages will materially alter which scenarios remain live.

races.name: Dubai Duty Free Irish European Breeders Fund Ragusa Handicap (Premier Handicap)

runners_data.name: Dawn Rising
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with a strong profile on Good ground and fair course form; the 25-day break is fine but from OR 99 needs a strong gallop to deliver a late run, which this race shape may not fully provide.

runners_data.name: This Songisforyou
runners_data.note: A 287-day layoff (23 jumps runs sandwiched in) is the dominant concern here — this hold-up type needs the race to be run at a true clip to finish past rivals, and first time back in this company that is a notable risk.

runners_data.name: In My Teens
runners_data.note: The confirmed front-runner who will dictate; runs out of her natural role at OR 96 here on a flat staying track, but her ability to control the fractions is the defining tactical factor for the whole field — headgear (h) worn.

runners_data.name: Cloud Seeker
runners_data.note: Trainer-ridden, consistently prominent and effective on Good ground; the step up to 1m4f from recent shorter assignments is worth monitoring but the strong course record and T14 figure of 4/33 suggest a live chance tracking the leader.

runners_data.name: The Real Screamer
runners_data.note: Two wins from two most recent starts, including a 1m2f win on Good — the slight concern is whether 1m4f stretches his stamina on quick ground, but the form is strong and a prominent position suits him perfectly here.

runners_data.name: Marazion
runners_data.note: Won over 1m2f on Good 14 days ago and that fitness edge is a genuine asset; prominent style fits the race shape well, and Foley is an astute jockey who will likely track In My Teens from a handy pitch — the headgear-free approach suits.

runners_data.name: Factual Fact
runners_data.note: De Bromhead's reliable stayer has placed second four times from five recent runs on Good ground, suggesting he finds plenty when asked but struggles to win — prominent to midfield and a strong stayer who will hit the board again.

runners_data.name: What's Your Game
runners_data.note: 90 days off and a limited record on truly Good going (0W1P in similar conditions) are both flags; a naturally prominent horse dropping slightly in OR, but the absence and going profile make him harder to trust here.

runners_data.name: Retracement
runners_data.note: A genuinely front-running type whose natural instinct is to race up with the pace — Ben Coen will try to slot him prominently, but with the field stacked up front he is likely to be shuffled wider and deeper than ideal, tempering his chance.

runners_data.name: Star Harbour
runners_data.note: Veteran hold-up horse (age 8) who wears a visor and has solid Good-ground form, including a recent second over 11f; the likely slow-run scenario does not play to his strengths and he will need the pace to lift significantly late.

runners_data.name: Obscenity
runners_data.note: Exciting young horse (4yo) with back-to-back wins on Good ground, showing real ability — his natural desire to race prominently will be squeezed in this congested field, and McCullagh's stable colleague Truth Be Told complicates his position.

runners_data.name: Truth Be Told
runners_data.note: Won back-to-back on Good ground over 1m and 1m2f; M C Grassick has no T14 entries (0/0), which is a slight concern for support, but the horse's own form is strong and he would be competitive if he can get a prominent pitch — 49 days off is fine.

runners_data.name: Navy Waters
runners_data.note: A five-year-old visor-wearer with strong staying form on Good and Heavy, including multiple placed efforts over 1m4f — naturally wants to race prominently but will be crowded back; W J Lee and 56-day break (22 jumps runs) are context.

runners_data.name: Railwayview Lady
runners_data.note: Wears a hood, hold-up filly dropping to OR 81 from a higher mark; the Good-ground record is solid (6/7 in similar conditions) but the two poor recent efforts (8-8) after wins suggest she may be coming into form again — one for late players if the pace lifts.

races.paceDynamic: In My Teens is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 14-runner field and, with no genuine rival willing to press from the outset, is expected to bowl along at a controlled, sustainable gallop over the 1m4f trip on Good to Firm ground at The Curragh. The early fractions will be honest but not fierce, creating a race that unfolds in a single-file procession through the middle stages before the tempo quickens turning for home. This shape — a lone leader setting a measured pace — classically benefits prominent-to-midfield stalkers who can track the gallop without expending energy fighting for position, then produce a sustained finish on the quick ground. Retracement, Truth Be Told, Obscenity, and Navy Waters are all genuine prominent racers but the field is too crowded at the head of affairs for all of them to secure their natural berth, so Cloud Seeker, The Real Screamer, and Marazion are best placed to actually race prominently behind In My Teens; hold-up horses face a stiff challenge if the pace does not truly collapse, making the close-tracking stalker profile the clear tactical beneficiary.

watchPoints.text: In My Teens' early gallop sets the entire tempo — if she is allowed to bowl along at a very comfortable clip unchallenged, prominent stalkers like The Real Screamer and Marazion will receive a near-perfect tow into the race and can pounce without burning a match.

Retracement, Truth Be Told, Obscenity, and Navy Waters are all natural prominent racers crammed into a congested early order — watch for bumping and checking in the first two furlongs as jockeys compete for limited berths behind In My Teens.

This Songisforyou's 287-day absence (with jumps runs in between) is a major fitness unknown; Colin Keane will likely settle this hold-up type quietly but a first run back in a Premier Handicap means he is unlikely to be fully wound up.

The going report confirms Good to Firm throughout the card at The Curragh — fast ground will place a premium on stamina reserves in the final two furlongs of this 1m4f trip, and horses with proven form on quick going (Dawn Rising 12/15, Cloud Seeker 13/15) hold a clear profile edge.

What's Your Game has been off 90 days and has a 0W1P record on comparable Good ground — the absence combined with the going profile makes him a significant question mark despite his competitive OR of 89.
